newsitem.title: USA: Xerox to unveil digital copier family.
newsitem.headline: Xerox to unveil digital copier family.

text.p: Xerox Corp. will unveil a full line of digital black-and-white copier products on Tuesday, an area that is becoming an increasingly important segment of its overall business, analysts said.
"This is a very important product announcement for them," said B. Alex Henderson, a Prudential Securities analyst. "It's a very important element of their corporate strategy."

A Xerox spokesman said it plans to unveil a new product family that will "lead to digital convergence in the office." Xerox Chief Eexecutive Officer Paul Allaire will also describe Xerox's strategy to enhance its digital product offerings and services.

Two months ago, Allaire told Wall Street analysts that Xerox's upcoming products would be easily upgradeable to act as high-speed, robust printers on networks. The copiers will also have better quality and reliability and have more features than other copiers currently available.
"Digital is where the future growth is," said Pete Enderlin, a Smith Barney analyst, adding that its digital products now make up about 30 percent of total revenues.
"They will account for all the growth going forward."
Analysts said a key element of the new products is that they provide a "baby step" to help customers move to digital.
Henderson said the new copiers will have multi-function capabilities, such as faxing, printing, scanning, copying and PC faxing, following in the steps of two earlier Xerox digital products.

"You are selling a networkable product, instead of a stand-alone product," Henderson said. A digital copier can be linked to a corporate computer network, instead of standing alone, unconnected to any other office equipment.
He said that the range in speeds of the new products is vast, going from eight pages a minute to 70 pages a minute.
Digital copiers represent big growth potential for Xerox.

Jonathan Rosenzweig of Salomon Brothers estimated in a recent report that digital product revenues will grow 22 percent in the company's first quarter. This compares with Xerox's total revenue growth of seven percent in the fourth quarter. Xerox is expected to report first quarter results on April 22.
While Xerox moves to embrace the digital world, analysts said it must continue to provide new products in the analogue area, which still makes up 55 percent of their revenues.
"They must also show they are not giving up the analogue product line," said Enderlin of Smith Barney.
